takeaways: Constellation earned $5.06 a share on an adjusted basis vs about $3.89 expected, and revenue of $9.55 billion topped the roughly $9.37 billion Street number (Benzinga). A year ago it made $3.04.

Much of the jump is the Calpine deal, which closed in January and roughly adds a fleet of gas plants to the nuclear business; the release also credits "favorable market and portfolio conditions." Share count rose to 354 million from 313 million, so per-share growth is not all free.
It raised the midpoint of full-year adjusted EPS guidance (the second raise this year) and narrowed the range to $12.50-$12.80.

The AI-power story kept stacking up: a 20-year, 690 MW deal with Amazon for Calvert Cliffs, a 20-year Google deal to add about 890 MW across 11 nuclear units, a new 270 MW "Peak+" contract, and a conditional DOE loan guarantee of up to $5 billion for nuclear uprates.
It also agreed to buy the 609 MW Rhode Island State Energy Center for $715 million. GAAP EPS was $5.19, so this was no accounting mirage in the other direction.
verdict: Constellation beat by more than a buck, raised guidance and kept signing Amazon and Google while it was at it. The stock was already up on Friday and the whole AI-power trade just got a wobble, so the real question is whether $5.06 was a peak or a floor. Max says the nukes are paying rent. Not advice.

sources.title: Benzinga: Constellation Q3 adj. EPS $5.06 beats $3.85 estimate
